rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 0 is still the best design (score 53.02). Across 240 development trials, none finished, and every run ended off track at progress 0.04 to 0.15 with max_error at the 0.06 m limit. Each run lost the line about once. Several factors have been tested against that baseline: kp 2.5 (35.5), kp 4.0 (50.8), 16 mm sensors (50.5), and sensor span ±0.06 m with other changes (50.6). The s-bend progress stayed at exactly 0.1475 across most changes, so the failure point is probably set by something the gains do not touch.

What I accept from the round-1 critique: (1) The sensor-span hypothesis is contradicted. Iteration 1 used ±0.06 m and the s-bend result did not move, so I drop the wider-array plan. (2) The draft changed six things at once and could not be attributed, so I return to the iteration-0 design exactly. (3) The factual error about iteration 4 is accepted: it scored 50.82, below iteration 0. (4) The base_speed cut to 1.4 is rejected, because it reduces the only route to the 500-point completion bonus and has no supporting evidence.

What I changed: one factor only. line_loss changes from last_direction to search_right. Every run ends with one line-loss event followed by an off-track exit, so the recovery behaviour after the line is lost is the one lever that acts directly on the observed terminal event. Everything else, including geometry, gains and base_speed 1.5, is identical to iteration 0, so any score change is attributable to line-loss recovery.

What I rejected: the critique's suggestion of a conservative start at much lower speed, because the data give no evidence that speed is the limit. I also did not test a gain change, since kp has now been tested at 2.5, 3.5 and 4.0 with 3.5 best, and kd and ki are untested alone.

Expected result: if the failure is in recovery after line loss, progress rises above 0.1475 on the s-bend and line_loss_events stays near 1. If the score is unchanged within about 0.05, the recovery direction is not the limit, and the next single test should be kd alone (0.15 to 0.4). If the score falls, revert to last_direction and test kd alone.

Decision rule for the next revision: if progress rises, keep search_right and test kd alone. If progress falls, revert to last_direction and test kd alone. If progress exceeds 0.9 with completion 0, raise base_speed by 0.1.
